evidence:
STATIC (source) ANALYSIS - frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r8/task; hashes of tests/scoring.toml (95f70d6e...), tests/tools/score.py (13de2b38...), scored/functional|polish|visual judge.toml (ae03cd30.../59114e63.../b4d4f206...) recomputed and match manifest.json. scoring.toml, score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty).
1) Aggregation is monotone non-decreasing in every criterion: score.py:40-48 reward = sum(w*dim)/sum(w) with weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2 (scoring.toml:5-8); each dimension is a RewardKit weighted_mean of non-negative weights (functional 43 criteria, total weight 58.5; polish 5, total 12; visual 5 likert, total 6.0). Gates (render, constraints) carry 0.0 mass and only zero the reward (score.py:41,48); the functional floor >0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11, score.py:47) is a step that only removes reward from the weaker side. No term is subtracted, so improving any single criterion never lowers reward.
2) Gates do not demand more than the brief and a stronger app does not fail them: gates/render/judge.toml (wrong password stays signed out; correct Recruiter signs in to a usable workspace); gates/constraints/judge.toml (Recruiter opens job with team, hiring manager, 2 places, adds candidate; Observer or any working staff account in an independent context sees exactly one Applied card) - all public (instruction.md:3,11,17; hireops_rules.md:11-12,27-36).
3) Function outweighs craft: functional 0.6 > polish+visual 0.4; visual (pure craft) is 0.2; polish rows are behavioural public promises (instruction.md:5,7; hireops_rules.md:115-175), not styling. The skill's inversion example (craft carrying more mass than function) does not occur.
4) Refusal/negative rows carry positive controls so a dead app cannot out-earn a working one on negatives: e.g. hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff ('A candidate who cannot sign in ... makes this row 0'), hro_anonymous ('A signed-in success of each is the control'), hro_candidate_private ('A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), hro_activity_refusals (successful lines are the control); functional/prompt.md:13 requires a same-kind positive control for every refusal row. Polish live rows score 0 if no update arrives, so a no-live-update app cannot earn preservation credit.
5) Status-code demands that could otherwise invert ranking against a stricter app are public: hro_anonymous 401 and hro_thread_access 'Noor's as not found' map to hireops_rules.md:21-23. hro_refused_put_back also accepts refusing before the card moves; move-refusal rows accept 'not offered' plus replay; hiding controls is optional. functional/prompt.md:19,23 and polish/prompt.md 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' limit cascade inversions.
TRIED: (a) broken app that could outrank a better one: a pretty app passing both gates with ~6% functional (just above the 0.05 floor) and visual 1.0 scores ~0.24, above an ugly app with functional 0.30 and visual/polish 0 (~0.18). That follows from the template-mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 + 0.05 floor profile (skill 'Delivery profile'; scoring.toml identical to template), and the 'better' app there is broadly illegible, so it is a Note, not a task defect. (b) conforming alternative that could fail: an app answering anonymous replays with 403 or a redirect would fail hro_anonymous, but 401 is public (hireops_rules.md:21); an app that also records notes in Activity is not failed by hro_activity (notes merely excluded). I found no criterion or gate that a strictly better conforming app fails while a worse one passes.
UNMEASURED RISK (reason for Not exercised / risk=true): ranking under the real configured judge has never been run. raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its only entries are scripted golden observations (workspace.json sha a424b50f... verified), explicitly 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'. A concrete inversion mechanism remains plausible and unrefuted: the functional judge must walk protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D for 43 criteria in one batched session (functional/prompt.md:21-51) under timeout=9000 (functional/judge.toml) inside test.sh's 11100 s scored budget (test.sh:224; functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 run serially with --max-concurrent-agent 1). A fully working app makes the judge execute every step (more replays, 15 s waits, restart), while a broken app fails fast; if the stronger app exhausts the budget, test.sh:224-225 exits leaving the gates-phase reward 0.0 (score.py:42-48 with no scored reward.json), or unobserved rows become binary 0 ('NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation', functional/prompt.md:53), so a better app could score below a worse one. No golden-vs-mutant ordering run exists to show the judge ranks consistently on the 15-second live/timing rows either. REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires hash-bound reward-ordering and workload records before clearance; these are missing and cannot be waived.
counterexample: No demonstrated inversion from weights, gates or criteria (static analysis). Unrefuted runtime scenario: a complete conforming app drives the batched functional judge through every protocol step and exhausts the 9000 s judge / 11100 s scored budget (test.sh:224-225), yielding reward 0.0 or NOT-EXERCISED zeros, while a broken app whose features fail fast finishes and keeps a positive reward. Not measured either way.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, run the full configured verifier on the golden and on graded mutants (e.g. no-live-updates, no-bulk/undo, leaky-candidate, pretty-but-thin) and record hash-bound reward-ordering and workload/duration evidence showing golden > partial > broken with no budget exhaustion; if the golden approaches the budget, reduce protocol scope rather than relying on an unmeasured timeout.
